photos.caption: Vermiculite insulation particle size relative to paper clip

lead: Vermiculite is a pebble-like, pour-in product, usually grey-brown or silver-gold, lying loose between the attic joists.
how: Look from the hatch with a torch. Do not reach in, sweep or scoop a sample.
Vermiculite is loose granules, from fine grains to pieces nearly an inch long, with a shiny, mica-like sheen. It pours; it does not hang together.
Not vermiculite: fiberglass batts or fluff (pink, yellow or white, like cotton candy), blown cellulose (grey, like shredded paper), mineral wool (woolly fibres).
Do not open walls to look for it. EPA advises against it.
verdict: If in doubt, do not disturb it — use an accredited tester. EPA goes further: treat any vermiculite insulation as if it contains asbestos, without testing.
